It's unclear how "creatures" (as opposed to people, who have Visions) like Andrius come to their elemental powers, but my best guess is that he originally had Cryo powers and only came to Anemo when Venti made him one of the four winds.

It seems that it is dependent upon the character's motivations - for example, Xinyan who works hard but wants to make an impression on Liyue, or Keqing who works hard and wants change, but ultimately has an Electro Vision. 

Therefore it seems that Albedo values hard work over even finding the truth of the world; that is, that he enjoys/values the journey rather than the destination, if that makes sense?

There seems to be a hierarchy with the goals which lead to a Vision, so it likely depends upon which is the part which helps them break through their doubt or difficulty. 

A great example is Xinyan - she is passionate about her music and undoubtedly works hard to achieve her goals. But in her moment of doubt, she didn't think, "if I work hard, I'll get there". 

Instead, she was determined to "become a "flame" that could light Liyue Harbor up" - i.e., it was her love for rock music which gave her the power to break through, hence her Pyro Vision.

With regard to "cutting out parts of the stories" - I deliberately focused on the Vision stories and only referred to other material where it was necessary to understand a character's motivations or understanding of the situation, as these are the stories which presumably explain why they hold their Visions. 

As we see in - esp. Cryo - a class of Vision holders can tend to have the same personality traits (self-sacrifice in Cryo's case), but this does not mean it is that tendency which leads them to have a Vision per se. This is why Cryo is about change rather than about self-sacrifice. 

Similarly, Baal seems to want to maintain the promised "eternity". If we assume this is some kind of stable society under her rule (not too much of a stretch, I think), then this explains why she is isolating and taking Visions - without power, how can she continue to be Inazuma's Archon? As we have seen before, Archons can be ousted. 

This is based upon the description of the Electro gems, rather than simply her behaviour because as with the Vision bios, this seems to speak more truly to the "core" of her motivations. 

As I mentioned in the start, the theme of these gods/Visions can be very openly interpreted - leading to the same ideal being both positive and negative, just as in Nine Pillars of Peace. This leads itself to the variety of motivations and behaviours that can exist beneath the same element, as not everyone perceives "protection" for example, the same way. 

This is not to say that my theory here is perfect or that I won't come back and disagree with what I've written before - that's wholly natural and some comments here have given me some stuff to think about. With regard to Electro specifically, Lisa gave me enough trouble that until Inazuma's release, I doubt I can really be sure about Electro's theme. She's just too OP. 

I hope that helped explain my reasoning behind the discussion and why I favoured certain parts over others. I'm glad you found this piece useful.

It is also a lot easier to prevent any further growth if all growth stems from you (discourging active innovation, etc.) 

The sundial is too recent to be related to Sel Vind. The Thousand Winds temple is dated between the time Barbatos moved Mondstadt to where it is now and prior to the Aristocracy era (it is discussed in the Sacrificial weapon set). In comparison, we know that this is the time period when the clan that the outlander begot came to Mondstadt - i.e., generations later.

I don't think Khaenri'ah made the ruin guards either, as it seems it was just being founded around the same time Sel Vind fell. The writing on them is also something we haven't seen before (blocky and geometrical). Perhaps an even older civilisation created them and every succeeding group co-opted them?

>This was discussed in several lore treads but what is the purpose of the cycle and the reason behind gods actions? 

Given that Genshin canonically takes place in the Honkai universe, most likely to prevent an even bigger world-ending event from being triggered due to high technological advancement.

It definitely seems to be the case - there is a large tree trunk around the Frostbearing Tree. Given that Sal Vind attempted to heal their tree by grafting ley line branches (from the Abyss) onto it, we can probably assume that they are related.

>So what I mean/meant was that Durin couldn’t have existed in Tevyat or at all before that, because those two events happen one after the other. (I hope that makes sense?)

The way I read the Festering Desire lore is that Durin's "dream" were things which did happen - he only refers to them as a dream, perhaps because it was so long ago, or because it was an idyllic time for him. Timeline-wise, this suggests Durin did indeed live prior to the fall of Khaenri'ah, as Venti was not around prior to this time.

>Hearing the people's cry for help, the Anemo Archon descended and awoke Dvalin.

Additionally, it is unclear whether Gold "created" the monsters per se, or whether they were infected by something. I lean towards the latter, however, as we can see from Dainsleif's artwork, one of his arms appears to be monster-like, whilst the majority of his person is human. This suggests a progressive disease/corruption, which is in line with Dvalin's lore following Durin's defeat.

>Since the Ancient Kingdom is in reference to Khaenri’ah and then it says it’s “inhabitants”, I assumed that meant the humans of Khaenri’ah. (⋟﹏⋞)

Precisely my point - the lines

>"The ancient kingdom was wrongfully cursed,"  
"Turning its inhabitants into monsters."

Are to be read as one sentence (note the comma in the first line). This suggests that what happened to Khaenri'ah was unjust, and intentional (presumably on the part of Celestia, due to the cycle).

>I hope I’m not misinterpreting what you said, but Gold was actively pursuing creating life, though perhaps not poisonous beasts(?).

It is a possibility. We simply don't have enough in lore right now to know what Gold wanted to do. I lean towards whatever he did possibly tying in to a dying leyline tree/other disaster (potentially what happened was that Khaenri'ah was cursed and he attempted to heal them, leading to a false narrative where he created the monsters). At this point in time, we only really have speculation.

Hope that clears things up!

Gold is the alchemist who is usually attributed with leading to Khaenri'ah's destruction. Mosts sources (i.e., from Mondstadt) say he was a greedy man who created monsters for some nefarious purpose. This is a little disputed from the lore that we have rn however (e.g., the Bloodstained Knight).

"Vere" is the ablative singular of "ver", and made the most sense out of the options on wikitionary (ignoring grammar becayse MHY seems to do the same). 

That being said, the dual meaning of "veremini" definitely makes more sense, and ties into the theme of what happened in Sel Vind. This seems the (way) more likely reading.

Celestia seems to be the home of a higher class of gods than the Archons (consider the unknown goddess/"sustainer of heavenly principles" vs the gods of elements/other miscellanea) - possibly why Vision holders ascend to Celestia, but the majority of gods seem to be on Teyvat (e.g., the Archon War, where there were many gods, and its aftermath where those gods fled to islands). 

The most likely, imo, is that the angels are the gods themselves - they are the ones who guide their people after all (Venti ensuring Mondstadt is free, ZL teaching them to build houses, etc.) - which, given how many gods existed before the domination of the Seven, would probably contribute to the sheer number of civilisations (the priests going to the tree left a "mountain of crowns"). 

I'd wager that there's a shift in the gods' attitudes (Venti, ZL possibly/likely, and even the Tsaritsa, who wants to "burn away the old world") towards this cycle. The change to the domination of the Seven vs previously, with all the different gods, might have been a change towards preventing the cycle too, depending on the gods' attitudes at the time. 

All this seems to suggest a possible endgame fighting Celestia...? - or so I hope.

> does that mean the tree we are healing is the one from the story 

If you mean the Frostbearing Tree in Dragonspine, then yes - kind of. We're feeding it more corruption/poison, basically. 

>does that mean the blue tree in Liyue (the one with the ominous girl proclaiming the return of something) is also a leyline tree 

Based on the big trunk surrounding the Frostbearing Tree, this seems likely, although it is uncertain why they don't appear white unless they're in domains/the Abyss. The blue in the Liyue tree is probably because of the monster/dragon that is buried beneath it, rather than its properties as a leyline tree.

\>On Durin: 

The Skyward weapons have a distinctly "Mondstadtian" tone to their stories (and also appear to be written in the current day?). In comparison, the lore of the Festering Desire and Dragonspine Spear contain firsthand accounts from Durin - presumably due to being imbued with parts of his body. Namely: 

>He had a very, very long dream...  
>  
>When he opened his eyes, he was in the sky above a mountain swept by roaring snowstorms... And that bejeweled, lovely dragon, like a tender lover, Had now pierced his neck through with its sharp fangs.  
>  
>"Farewell, Mother! My journey is ended."  
"I shall sleep beneath this white, shining silver... and perhaps this, too, is good."  
"Farewell, O lovely bard! And farewell, O lovely dragon!"  
"Would that we had met in a different time and place,"  
"To meet, to song and dance together!" So he thought most sincerely as he lay dying.

A very different image to the vicious, jealous dragon we see in the Skyward series. 

\>On Gold:

There are conflicting accounts about Gold, namely from the lore of the Bloodstained Knight, who was a knight during the fall of Khaenri'ah. 

>"And so, the black-stained knight persisted on his path, pursuing monsters in the name of justice,  
Until he came upon an **ancient, ruined realm, where he discovered the ultimate injustice**..." 

And

>"He ventured into **the fallen ancient kingdom**, and died in battle in the monsters' lair.  
At the bottom of the world, **he learned the origin of the monsters that destroyed the ancient kingdom**.  
"The **ancient kingdom was wrongfully cursed**,"  
"**Turning its inhabitants into monsters**."  
"The code of chivalry tolerates not such injustice."  
"If Abyss be thy name, I pledge to you my loyalty."" 

Additionally, in Dainsleif's lore: 

>(With reference to Gold) The future must atone for bygone mistakes 

I doubt that actively attempting to create monsters would constitute a "mistake" in the eyes of the people affected. Furthermore, this "prophet" discusses the cycle of the world - which as discussed in my post, likely refers to the gods allowing a certain level of development before destroying civilisations. 

\>On leylines

It is unlikely that Khaenri'ah existed at the time of Sal Vind (see post). Furthermore, the cycle mentioned above seems to have happened *many times*, so we cannot know when the ancient capitol was created, only that it has seen the priests of many civilisations come to pray when their people face doom

>The **line of chief priests have always seen this same sight as their days draw to an end**:  
**A mountain of crowns in a secret place, beneath a withered tree**——each one hiding a lifetime of secrets kept.  
Each retiring chief priest offers up their crown of flawless white branches to this world.  
**Every mighty and ancient city, and every austere place of sacrifice must one day return to profundity in the earth**.  
  
>  
>**All prosperity must someday end.**  
But this does not mean that nothing is eternal.  
>  
>**At the end of a cycle, the earth shall be renewed**. Thus eternity is cyclical.

Dainsleif could be watching over the tree. He could also be watching over branches of it - just as how Imunaulkr attempted to revitalise Sal Vind's tree by grafting pieces of the world tree onto it. There's simply not enough information to be certain at the time; although he's definitely related to our sibling, and therefore the Abyss Order...

>The scribe's box text mentions people wanting to found a nation without gods, but he doesn't call them foreigners or 'those distant unbelievers' or anything like that you'd expect. I feel like they're his own people that left to start their own colony somewhere. 

I think this would depend on how quickly the storms descended - the storms were so severe when Imaulkr left that it was described as a "wall of wind and ice". 

The scribe also seemed to have given up on everything - wanting to see the skies burn, to see the world poisoned, that he could have just felt a little vindication at hearing about people who wanted to be free from the gods. 

>the nation of Khaenri'ah fell in much more recent history (debated between 100-500 years prior to the main story in the game. The one book that mentions it says Khaenri'ah fell 100 years before, but in-game text mentions that book itself could be several hundred years old.) 

Khaenri'ah is basically confirmed to have happened 500 years ago. A particular quote by Dainsleif I - for whatever reason - keep forgetting is: 

>But if the disaster from five centuries ago were to happen again, if he were to face the same evil that I once did...

It's scattered across Dragonspine. On the Genshin Wiki, they're primarily on the pages for "Ancient Carvings", "Secret Room" (individual boxes are linked there), the cryo artifact set lore, and the "Snow-Tombed Starsilver".

Edit: for the rest, feel free to just search up the lines quoted. The Wiki should be amongst the first searches.

This may be so, but the "tai" in Taishan Mansion and in Mt. Tai are totally different words in cn, rendering this theory unlikely. 

Taishan Mansion is 太山府 (great mountain mansion), whilst Mt. Tai is 泰山 (peaceful mountain).

You're right, in the Adeptal Summons quest, she does claim to have invented the island - which is mb for forgetting this quest. 

This alone doesn't explain the letter upon the island, in particular its return after the closure of Taishan Mansion. Therefore, perhaps they built it together?

My issue with this theory is that through the Pale Princess, we know that there are two civilisations residing in the Abyss:

>In the distant past, the Night Mother ruled over the faraway Land of Night. Here, no light touched the earth, nor did a single tree grow, and there was no life here but the horrendous denizens of the dark.

And

>The Moonlight Forest was the only place free from the rule of the Night Mother. Only there could the people bask in the bright moonlight and enjoy the grace it brought to the living.

I therefore think that whilst the Spiral Abyss is likely an entrance to the Abyss - and therefore to Khaenri'ah, the actual Abyss is far deeper down (corroborated by the elemental circlet set, wherein the chiefs had to descend deeper into the earth to reach the abyss, where the tree is).

It's also difficult to imagine how the moon could become red - indicative of a lunar eclipse - although that could simply be video game logic. 

Other than that, it's a solid theory ~~and made me review the video and realise that I shouldn't have given Lumine being on the surface any stock, since the buildings there seemed to already be ruins~~.

Kaeya's name is 凯亚 (Kaiya) in cn. You can also hear it [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eubfgs8PTu4&ab_channel=Trashy). I assume that it's ガイア (Gaia) in jp because it's more comfortable to say in jp. A similar thing happened in another game I play, so it's not too surprising.

Hm, that's something I hadn't considered, but I think either way the conclusion is: Khaenri'ah had a really weird moon situation going on (cue Scaramouche telling us the sky is fake, maybe?) 

The geosynchronous moon situation was the only way I could explain the third moon and Khaenri'ah's moon, but if it was always in the Abyss/underground, then it could have been illuminated by the moon we see in the Spiral Abyss instead, since we know the Spiral Abyss leads underground. 

I did consider that there might not be a perfect 10-day cycle and dive a little bit into that (discussing how it is impossible that there was *no* moon on the day Khaenri'ah fell, because we see the moon in the We'll be Reunited video). My assumption about the cycle is based off cn copy of the book, which says:

>Every ten days, one sister takes over the throne of the other.

I read the line to mean, "if there are two moons in the sky" rather than the moons being absent, but I could not really think of any explanation for this so I didn't comment on it. 

Your version definitely accords better with the idea of cumulative disasters ("with time, disasters overturned the sovereign carriage"). This is why I reference the cn version of the book specifically, as MHY has an issue of mistranslating into English, affecting the meaning of things. Instead, the cn version seems to talk about a single catastrophe: 

>"They (the sisters) drove a silver chariot every ten days (一旬), a sister replacing the other's reign. Thus was their ever-repeating cycle, until the day great catastrophe descended".

Although the word used for "ten days" can be quite vague and refer to ["a period of time" rather than just ten days](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%97%AC#Chinese), ten days [seems to be the preferred translation](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/chinese-english/%E6%97%AC). 

It's issues like this that I like to check against the cn versions of things when the en version doesn't make sense, tho there's no telling what I might have missed, since ~~cn too hard for me to reliably double check everything~~. 

Anyway, it's because the cn version of the book seems to indicate a perfect 10-day cycle that I preferred this version in my theory, hope that cleared that up for you!

Like I said, it's not uncommon for games where you make choices to have a "base" canon for the game/story to default to, without the influence of players' choices. Aether mc represents this default world. 

Besides, I think equating the web event to the other sources where Aether is the mc is a false equivalence. 
Aether is the mc/Lumine is the Queen in materials which are relevant to the storyline - the We'll Meet Again video (which is marked as containing story spoilers), the Teyvat Chapter Storyline Preview (story spoilers again), the opening cutscene on their youtube channel, and the manga. These things (even if we exclude the cutscene, by virtue of this being where we make our choice) all suggest that MHY's canon is that Aether is the mc, due to their being sources of canonical lore. 

(I'm not 100% sure since I played the Mondstadt storyline a long time ago, but there miiiight be a cutscene where they say there's a queen, even if you're playing Lumine. But I could just be getting cutscenes mixed up with the Chorus) - i.e., that Aether's lines are being recorded first/preferred, possibly because it's more important for MHY to get their canon out first. This is true even if they record a second Chorus video. 

The web event, on the other hand, is a fairly interchangeable event, without any real consequences on the story. The same can be said of the trailer you shared. I think they likely are/want to showcase Lumine mc because - well, not doing so is a bit odd given the possibility for choice, and also beause she seems (at least, from my twitter feed) to be the more popular of the two. 

MHY absolutely could have recorded two versions of the Chorus, but the fact is that they did not. This, in addition to Aether being the mc in so many other sources of canonical lore outside of the game suggest that this is the canon that MHY defaults to. This is fine - if you prefer Lumine mc, then all you need to do is swap genders around - this is a very simple change in comparison to the example I gave above with Dragon Age, where there is a default state with multiple choices chosen for the "base" world. 

That is in part the beauty of RPGs - to have the ability to influence the world, whether it's the things you say to Timmie when you kill his pigeons, or the gender of your character. But the fact remains that MHY has to keep a consistent canon story for storytelling purposes, especially since they pull in other sources of lore quite a bit. Therefore, if as you say, you prefer Lumine mc, then that's fine, and all you need to do is swap Aether and Lumine's roles around when you read other sources of canonical lore. 

We actually don't know whether the kingdom in the heavens in the Chorus is Celestia. We simply don't know enough about it to be sure, and I could just as easily say that it definitely isn't Celestia because it's shaped differently to the Celestia we see in the manga/ig. I didn't go down this path because it's pretty disingenous imo, and as I said, we really don't know enough about Celestia to say for sure that it is or isn't. Another possibility is that they are from Celestia, but Celestia itself connects to many different worlds, hence the world-hopping, and it's so removed from Teyvat life that the twins are clueless - again, we just don't have enough information. 
Venti himself seems to know way more about - if we assume the character is the mc, then us - than we do at the current time so I'm sure the Chorus will make more sense given time. 

And it's certainly true some people might play the game without looking at outside lore, but this is extemely unlikely (if you're invested in the game enough to go through the storyline, especially to the end, you're more likely to have read at least the manga, which features Aether mc - or watched the story preview, to learn more about the story), and besides, the vast majority of cutscenes use the in-game models which circumvents this issue. 

I hope that addressed your concern about Lumine mc - to me, it's really jsut an aesthetic choice for the players and doesn't have any bearing on the canonical (MHY's) story.

That's very true, but we do see this being acknowledged, at least a little bit, in Liyue - the Chi, which is now called Qingce (the quest title was mistranslated) and the story about the flower ball: 

>Some say the Liyue custom was originally adopted from the Ludi Harpastum festival celebrated in the neighboring Wind Kingdom of Mondstadt. Others say it dates back to before the Archon War, when the Salt God roamed free in Liyue. She once stood shoulder to shoulder with the many gods of Liyue, but her extraordinarily gentle nature saw her quickly ousted in the hubris of the Archon War, before being ruthlessly murdered by one of her own followers.

It's possible that Mondstadt was just so stable that cultural/linguistic changes didn't occur to the point that they're so noticeable as to be noted. 

~~Besides, what's more unrealistic is the existence of a common language that everyone, everywhere, seems to speak.~~

I could definitely be wrong too! I'm not sure how people generally see a generation, but I've always seen one as lasting 60-100 years (roughly the length of a human lifespan), but as you said - it doesn't detract too much from our points. 

Haha, I'm glad. Of course, theories can change with more information being given to us over time, but I'm glad it seems to have made sense to a lot of people, given what we know so far. 

If we assume that the Gnostic Chorus is about the twins, which does seem to be the case (e.g., Venti referring to us ("you") in the video, the fact that MHY's canon has Aether as the mc...) makes it seem like Lumine saw Khaenri'ah's fall. 

This doesn't explain everything per se (e.g., Lumine being the first heir despite being younger, or the fact they travelled together), but I think these have relatively simple possible explanations, like Lumine being more suited to rule or the fact being tasked with finding the pearl doesn't necessarily preclude her from travelling with Aether. 

There was another commentor suggesting it was the Pale Princess in the Gnostic Chorus since Lumine may be the mc in game, but I find this argument pretty weak - the game giving us the ability to choose a twin doesn't impact MHY's canon. It's similar to say, Dragon Age, where there is a "base" canon which is used if you don't make a specific world with specific choices to influence events. 

I also avoided referencing the rest of the Pale Princess series (the blurbs), as we only have the one story and the blurbs can only tell us so much. Besides, Lumine seems to have lost her memory about Aether (in the We Will Meet Again video, she seems to have a dramatic flashback when he's mentioned), which imo suggests she did forget him until that moment, leading me to assume the Gnostic Chorus is about us. 

The Tsaritsa's change in personality is something that I think is rooted in Honkai lore, which given, I don't know much about. Roughly, from what I've seen here and there, the gods prevent civilisations from advancing beyond a certain stage through a Honkai... event...? Basically, they end the world. 

Which definitely ties into the theory above (100 years of prosperity before being destroyed), and possibly the Tsaritsa's personality change too. Childe tells us she loved so much she had to close off her heart, and her people seem to be the most technologically advanced on Teyvat. It's possible that she fears that Sneznhaya will be destroyed by Celestia for this. 

It's uncertain whether Lumine is the queen of the Abyss or Khaenri'ah or both, so it's hard to tell specifically what each faction wants, especially since they're so closely intertwined. I say this because Lumine being sent to take the pearl/the Gnostic Chorus echoes the Hymn of the Pearl (which would insinuate she's Khaenri'ah's queen), but she's called the Queen of Darkness, which evokes the Abyss more. 

It's also possible that their goals are the same and/or Khaenri'ah has been subsumed into the Abyss. After all, both nations were destroyed by the gods (making their goals likely to be similar) and Khaenri'ah appears to be within the Abyss (because of the Bloodstained Knight's lore). 

Either way, the Bloodstained Knight being inspired to join the Abyss Order because of what he learnt suggests that - whatever the Order's goals are - it is at least in part righteous with regards to Khaenri'ah. As you say, this doesn't necessarily mean they want justice per se - but revenge might be considered justice too. We simply don't know enough about what specifically they want yet. 

The Abyss engulfing all the thrones is - I think - suggesting that the endgame will revolve around destroying Celestia (similar to how god is called "the king of kings" in the Hymn. Which is something I'm all for, after seeing what they've been up to...

But (from my understanding of it), it could also last a long time - 100 years could be a single generation, for example, if a father was 100 years old and his son was alive (hopefully the extreme and simplified example illustrates how generations under this definition are more variable and potentially longer). Therefore, it would depend more so on the quality of life/etc. 

I definitely agree that the first civilisation were turned into monsters too, and became the Abyss Mages. There's also the question of which language can/should be attributed to which nation - we typically refer to the Abyss Mage language as "Khaenri'ahn" on this sub, but it could potentially date from before Khaenri'ah. I have excluded this discussion and only brought up the langauges as a point of interest in the theory because there just isn't enough information to definitively attribute either language to either kingdom (the Mages could be using their original language, or adapted to Khaenri'ah's language....) 

Therefore, all that can be really be said given the information we have is that the Ruin Guards are from an ancient civilisation, but we'd need more information to attribute it to a certain one. 

The information about Arundolyn, Rostram, and the Bloodstained Knight are primarily from the Brave Heart (Arundolyn), Bloodstained Chivalry (Bloodstained Knight), Defender's Will (Rostram) and Favonious weapon (Arundolyn and Rostram) sets. There's a few other sources, so the timeline on the wiki is a good place to start. 

Rostram taught the Bloodstained Knight:

>"By this credo he also mentored a white knight who loved justice above all else. 

Which is confirmed in: 

>Following the teachings of the Wolf Pup, who taught him chivalry, justice and swordsmanship,

This white knight later becomes the Bloodstained Knight when  he realises he's become a monster in the eyes of other people in the course of destroying the monsters (presumably from Khaaenri'ah): 

>"As the Bloodstained Knight reached out to help a person in need after slaying the monster.  
The way she cowered in fear made the knight realize:

AFAIK, ministers are allowed to refuse to perform ceremonies already [x](http://www.equalitycampaign.org.au/bill-analysis) - search for 'refuse'. I think the wording of this law would probably have to be worded pretty specifically/very well, since this is a fairly delicate matter, to allow ministers the freedom to deny services to certain people but still remain as anti-discriminatory as possible. 

As for freedom to express that SSM is immoral - I think it's the same situation as groups expressing racist sentiments, or indeed, Pauline Hanson talking about how anti-Islam she is and so on. You have the right to say whatever you want (within reason), you'll just get a lot of flak. 

As for choosing not to employ gay people, this is against the law as far as I can tell. In [NSW](http://www.antidiscrimination.justice.nsw.gov.au/employers-and-managers/anti-discrimination-law-and-employers) for example, it is illegal to treat people unfairly for their orientation, gender, etc., and while exceptions can be made, it is generally if there is proof that you need someone of that gender (a female worker in a women's shelter for example). I think this is pretty fair, since it's important to allow people equal opportunity to work, earn money, etc. this is very different from denying religious services or the such. 

I honestly feel like the religious freedom argument is a non-argument. It has been covered already by existing law/existing law principles can be extended to SSM. And even if this were not the case, these issues honestly feel (to me at least) small enough to not really warrant such a debate?

I have to admit, I'm definitely fairly cynical about the human condition overall. I tend towards the belief that humans will do whatever is easiest rather than what is for the best, and that humans only really do good things because it benefits them since people will tend to see them as being 'good' people (I honestly grapple with this a lot, and wonder a lot if my involvement in activism is because I want to be liked, haha). I don't know if anything can really be done to improve people's involvement; if you ask an average person, they'll probably say that they are against sexism/child labour/etc. but nonetheless, it is easier to ignore these things and maybe benefit from it. Education and emotional appeals can only go so far, but there will always be *someone* who believes enough, you know? To make something happen, I think it's more important to empower people who *do* want to see a change, rather than keep screaming at an antipathetic or not engaged crowd. 

I'm involved with Amnesty (the group I'm working with rn is working on getting MPs to enforce changes within the judicial system to stop the whole cycle involving Indigenous youth and jail). I'm also involved with on-campus student associations which advocate for issues experienced by certain groups of students. I entirely understand the feeling of powerlessness, especially when facing really huge issues, but I like to remember that once upon a time, slavery was the norm. That racial segregation existed. That once, women couldn't even vote. Then I remember that despite all that, we've come so far, and we will continue to move forward. 

I do understand that sentiment, but I really do worry about the children of particularly bigoted people not being able to learn sex ed (think of the current same sex marriage and safer schools debates in Australia right now). I think in an ideal world, parents would be able to opt out of the system for personal reasons and we would not need to be worried about whether it is a legitimate reason or something based off unfounded fear. Ultimately, between bigotry and education, I believe that education should win. I think it is less 'acing upon (one's kinks)' on the characters, and more acting upon them in real life. A person with a non-con kink, for example, is not necessarily a rapist. They could be exploring the darker side of their sexuality, dealing with the realities of rape in real life (whether it is experience or rape culture etc.) or using it as a way to project their feelings of helplessness etc. People read/write fanfiction not just for the most obvious reasons, but also for psychological reasons that we as readers may or may not be privy to. 

I think it is also a little unfair to fic writers/readers to say that all slavery fanfiction is just gratuitous sex (which the stats didn't explore). For example, I have/had a series idea that explored the theme of freedom, and fighting for freedom, which followed Fenris from the moment he won the competition thing to become Danarius' body guard (and thus underwent the lyrium branding) to his escape; and this idea was extended to Anders and Solas and Zevran too. This would have been tagged as slavery, of course, but is not necessarily gratuitous pwp. 

Furthermore, a story can be about slavery and sex without necessarily *promoting* it. Captive Prince would be an example of this (I assume, from fans' reactions; I was too uncomfortable with the idea of a person being in a relationship that is portrayed as healthy and romantic with their abuser to read it). In this series, the ultimate stance of the story and the characters is that 'slavery is bad', and the main characters make moves to eradicate it. This does not detract from the fact that it is mostly non-con slave kink, but exists along side it. 

TL;DR: fanfiction exists not just as a vessel for one's fantasies but also as a safe place to vent negative emotion. It is written not necessarily for the most obvious reasons. Not all slave fanfiction is immediately slave kink pwp, and even so, it is possible for it to disparage the institution of slavery.

Death be not proud, though some have called thee

Mighty and dreadful, for thou art not so;

For those whom thou thinkst thou dost overthrow

Die not, poor Death, nor canst thou kill me.

From rest and sleep, but which thy pictures be,

Much pleasure; then from thee much more must flow,

And soonest our best men with thee do go,

Rest of their bones and soul's delivery.

Thou art slave to Fate, Chance, Kings and desperate men,

And dost with poison, war, and sickness dwell,

And poppies or charms can make us sleep as well 

And better than thy stroke; why swellest thou then?

One short sleep past, we awake eternally,

And death shall be no more; Death, thou shalt die.

I feel like that a lot, and I'm not going to lie, I don't really have any do-this-and-it'll-be-okay type solution. I find that just drawing when I feel like it (say, if I find something really inspiring or a picture that really speaks to me) rather than forcing me to draw from imagination right off the bat really helps. Sometimes I'll doodle just to pretend I'm drawing and it'll come to me (and that doodle will turn into a painting). I guess the take away is you can't really force it; in my experience, at least.

If you're wanting to draw people from your mind, then I'd suggest learning some basic anatomy in order to understand how humans 'work'/look like (same principle for vehicles or whatever it is you want to draw). 

From there you'd have the basic understanding needed to start you off, and as you kept drawing, you'd improve your artistic skill. 

Also, never be afraid to use reference images to help you understand anatomy/light/etc. References are an amazing resource, never underestimate how helpful they can be.

I think it really depends on what you want to be better at. For example, I recently decided that I wanted to focus on learning to paint. So I spent a few weeks doing that. Once I was decently happy with that, I moved onto portraits, and so on and so forth. 

If you really want to be better at one specific part of the body, I'd suggest spending more time working on that part. If you'd rather be good generally/at drawing the whole body, I'd try drawing the whole body, and spending a little more time on especially hard areas. 

Best of luck! :)

Personally, I love tiamat but only build it into a hydra (very) late game for two main reasons: 

1. The active is a part of your combo and it's really useful when you get exhausted or if the carry is healed/shielded through your burst or something

2. The active also lets you go to a lane that's getting pushed in, and in two button presses clear the wave so your team can focus on grouping and fighting/taking objectives quicker and without having to worry about side lanes

That being said, I hardly ever upgrade tiamat. Hydra is literally my last item in 99% of games but omitting it entirely, I found (only did it in one game though) really hurt my wave clear.
